items.text: Under the Oregon Psilocybin Services Act, adults 21 and over can use psilocybin at a licensed service center without a prescription or referral, after a preparation session with a licensed facilitator. Products can't be bought to take away; it isn't a dispensary model.

laws.rule: Visitors 21 and over may buy cannabis from OLCC-licensed retailers with ID and carry up to 2 ounces of usable cannabis in public. Public use is illegal, including streets, sidewalks and parks; use only on private property with the owner's permission. Cannabis remains illegal under US federal law, including on federal land.

Oregon's State Fire Marshal says only 'retail' (consumer) fireworks are legal for the public, such as fountains, flitter sparklers, smoke devices, ground spinners, wheels and novelty devices. They may be sold from June 23 to July 6. The state sets no time of day or year for use, but fireworks are prohibited on Oregon beaches, in state parks and campgrounds, and on state and federal forest lands, and local governments can add limits. Items such as sky lanterns, missiles, rockets, firecrackers, cherry bombs, M-80s, Roman candles and bottle rockets are illegal without a state permit.

In Oregon state parks, campfires are allowed only in park-provided fire rings or fireplaces and in the parts of the beach where fires are allowed (dry, open sand away from grass and driftwood). Extra fire restrictions can apply and some parks ban campfires most summers. Explosives and fireworks are not allowed in state parks or on the ocean shore.
Oregon State Parks says visitors may bring alcohol to parks except where specifically banned, and some parks need written approval from the park manager. No one under 21 may possess or drink alcohol.

Oregon state park properties and the ocean shore are closed to drone operations unless approved by permit, other than a list of park properties open from 8 August 2026 without a permit. FAA rules apply at all times. Check the parks agency list before flying.

layers.process: For Multnomah Falls, a timed use permit was required to park in the I-84 parking lot (Exit 31) from 22 May to 7 September 2026, daily 9 am to 6 pm. The Forest Service page says reservations are required to visit in that window. An online timed permit cost a US$2.00 transaction fee (about A$2.85); a limited supply of free timed-use permits was available in person at the Gateway to the Gorge Visitor Center in Troutdale and the Cascade Locks Historical Museum. That 2026 window has ended, and the page read gives no 2027 dates, so check the Forest Service page and recreation.gov before a visit in warm months. Outside the window the permit is not listed as required. The page suggests car-free options such as Columbia Area Transit. Other rules on the same page: drone takeoffs and landings are prohibited at the site; pets on a leash; no bikes, e-bikes, scooters, skates or skateboards. Restrooms were closed for renovation through November 2026. Fees in US dollars; A$1 = USD 0.7040 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so US$1 is about A$1.42.
